2027-04-19.title: Monday after the Third Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: A new and living way through the curtain; do not neglect to meet together
The shepherd who goes after the one lost sheep
2027-04-19.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Third Sunday after the Resurrection. Yesterday the Church heard of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus.
2027-04-19.verse: Let us hold fast to the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who has promised is faithful.
theo: Christ is risen! Yesterday we walked with the two disciples to Emmaus and saw them run back to Jerusalem to find the others. Today the Letter to the Hebrews tells us what the risen Lord has opened for us: “we have confidence to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus, by the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain (that is, through his flesh).” In the temple at Jerusalem a curtain separated the Holy of Holies, and only the high priest passed through it, once a year. When Jesus died, “the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom” (Matthew 27:51). His own flesh, given on the Cross and raised on the third day, has become the doorway into the presence of God. In our churches the curtain of the sanctuary is drawn back as the Holy Qurbono begins, and the faithful see the altar opened before them. We may see in it a sign of what Christ has done: heaven is no longer closed. So the Letter invites us: “let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water,” words that recall our Baptism.

Then come three simple commands. “Let us hold fast to the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who has promised is faithful.” “Let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good deeds.” And: do not neglect “to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another.” Already in the first generation some Christians were drifting away from the Sunday assembly. The Gospel shows the heart of God for those who drift. Tax collectors and sinners are “coming near to listen” to Jesus, and some Pharisees and scribes grumble: “This fellow welcomes sinners and eats with them.” They were devout people, and their grumbling is a temptation that every religious person knows. Jesus answers with a story: a shepherd with a hundred sheep loses one, leaves the ninety-nine, goes “after the one that is lost until he finds it,” lays it on his shoulders, and calls his neighbours to rejoice. St Ambrose saw in the shepherd's shoulders the arms of the Cross, on which Christ carried our sins home (in substance).

Put the two readings together and a task appears. The new and living way is open; the shepherd is searching; and we are asked not to neglect meeting together, but to encourage one another. Who is missing from our Sunday Qurbono? Perhaps a young person who moved to a city for studies, a family hurt by some quarrel in the parish, an elderly person no longer able to walk to church, a neighbour who simply lost the habit. This week, be the shepherd's hands. Call one of them, visit, offer a ride, carry the Holy Qurbono's joy to those who cannot come by asking the priest to bring Holy Communion to the sick. And look into your own heart: if you are the one who has wandered, the Lord is not waiting at a distance to scold you. He is already on the road looking for you, and there is joy in heaven when you are found.
outline: Ask: who is missing from our Sunday assembly, and who is looking for them?
Point 1 · A new and living way
Through the curtain of his flesh, heaven is opened.
Point 2 · Do not neglect to meet together
Hold fast, provoke one another to love, encourage one another.
Until he finds it, and joy in heaven.
live: Phone or visit one person who has stopped coming to the Holy Qurbono, simply to tell them they are missed.
When someone returns to church or to the sacraments, welcome them warmly and without comment on the past.
2027-04-19.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen Shepherd, you opened for us a new and living way through the curtain of your flesh, and you go after every sheep that is lost until you find it. Give us a true heart and full assurance of faith. Keep us faithful to the confession of our hope, and make us eager to meet together, to provoke one another to love and good deeds, and to go out to those who have wandered. Carry home on your shoulders all who are lost, and fill heaven with joy. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: Through the flesh of Christ, torn on the Cross and risen in glory, the way into the sanctuary is open; at the Holy Qurbono we approach that sanctuary and receive his true Body and Blood.

quick: Through his flesh Jesus opened a new and living way into God's presence.
We must hold fast to our hope, encourage one another, and not neglect meeting together.
The Good Shepherd seeks the one lost sheep and rejoices when it is found.
2027-04-19.action: Contact one person who has drifted from church and tell them they are missed.
2027-04-19.question: Am I among those who grumble, or among those who go out to seek?

family.explain: A shepherd had a hundred sheep. One got lost. He left the others safe and went looking for the lost one until he found it. Then he carried it home on his shoulders, very happy, and called his friends to a party! Jesus is like that shepherd. When anyone is lost, he looks for them, and heaven is full of joy when they come back.
family.intention: We pray for someone we know who has stopped going to church.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family or street might feel lost or left out, and how can we help?”

illus: A Sunday school teacher in the Marthandam area noticed that a boy from her class had been absent for three Sundays. Others said, “He will come back when he wants to.” On the fourth Saturday she walked to his house. His father had lost his job, the family was ashamed, and the boy had no clean shirt for Sunday. She said nothing about the absences. The next morning she waited at the church gate, and when the boy came with his mother, she took his hand and walked him to his place in front. Years later the boy, by then a catechist himself, said that he had learned the parable of the lost sheep that morning, without a word of it being read.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you have opened the way to the Father. Gather us tonight and send us to seek those who are lost. Amen.
share: By the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain (Hebrews 10:20). What does it mean for me that heaven is open?
Not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some (Hebrews 10:25). Why do I need the Sunday assembly, and who needs me there?
He goes after the one that is lost until he finds it (Luke 15:4). Whom is the Lord asking me to seek?
pm.resp: Good Shepherd, seek and save the lost.
interc: For the Church, that she may always go out to seek those who have wandered.
For our parish, that no one may drift away unnoticed.
For young people who have moved away for studies or work, that they may find a home in the Church wherever they are.
For families hurt by quarrels in the parish, that they may be healed and return.
For the sick and the elderly who cannot come to church, that they may receive the Holy Qurbono at home.
pm.close: Father, through the flesh of your Son you have opened for us a new and living way. Make us faithful to the confession of our hope, eager to meet together and encourage one another, and send us with the Good Shepherd to seek the lost. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews says that Jesus opened for us a new and living way through the curtain, that is, through his flesh (Hebrews 10:20). At his death the curtain of the temple was torn. Heaven is open.

So we are told: let us hold fast to the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who has promised is faithful (Hebrews 10:23). Let us encourage one another, and not neglect to meet together, as is the habit of some.

In the Gospel the shepherd leaves the ninety-nine and goes after the one that is lost until he finds it. He does not scold; he lays it on his shoulders and rejoices. St Ambrose saw in those shoulders the arms of the Cross (in substance).

Yesterday we heard how the Emmaus disciples ran back to the community. Today let us look for those who have not come back. Call one of them; visit; bring them with you. And if you are the lost one, know that the Shepherd is already on the road looking for you. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever lost something you loved and searched everywhere for it? Jesus told a story about a shepherd who lost one sheep. He searched and searched until he found it, then carried it home on his shoulders and had a party! Jesus loves every one of us like that. If a friend stops coming to Sunday school, can you tell them: we miss you?

intro: Theme: “He who has promised is faithful.”
On the Monday after Emmaus Sunday: the new and living way, the assembly we must not neglect, and the shepherd who searches.

sub: The curtain of the temple torn.
Through his flesh, given and raised.
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts
At that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.
points.apply: When the sanctuary curtain is drawn back at the Holy Qurbono, thank Christ for opening heaven to you.

points.h: Do not neglect to meet together
sub: Hold fast to the confession of hope.
Encourage one another as the Day approaches.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
points.apply: Never miss the Sunday Qurbono this Easter season, and encourage one other person to come.

sub: Joy in heaven over one sinner.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Visit or call one person who has wandered from the parish, and tell them they are missed.

concl: Through the flesh of the risen Christ the way into God's presence is open.
The Shepherd seeks the lost; we are sent to seek them with him and to welcome them home with joy.
2027-04-19.resolve: This week, bring one wanderer one step nearer to the Sunday assembly.
